data.text:
🌀 Tropical Depression #Jangmi Update:

— Tropical Depression Jangmi continues tracking generally north to northwest over the western Pacific Ocean and is expected to gradually strengthen over warm waters in the coming days. Current forecast guidance suggests the system will likely remain east of the Philippines before curving toward the Ryukyu Islands south of Japan.

For the Philippines, a direct LANDFALL is not expected at this time. However, outer rainbands and an enhanced southwest monsoon flow could still bring periods of heavy rain, gusty winds, rough surf, and dangerous marine conditions to portions of eastern Luzon and the northern Philippines. Residents should continue monitoring updates, especially for possible flooding, landslides, and hazardous seas. 

People in Taiwan should also closely monitor the progress of Jangmi, as forecast models indicate the storm may pass near or east of the island while strengthening. Even without a direct LANDFALL, Taiwan could experience increased rainfall, rough coastal surf, dangerous rip currents, gusty winds, and localized flooding, especially across eastern and northern areas. Any westward shift in the forecast track could bring stronger impacts closer to the island. 

The current projected track takes Jangmi toward the Ryukyu Islands of southern Japan, where impacts could become more significant later in the forecast period. Forecast guidance currently suggests a possible approach and LANDFALL near Okinawa and the Ryukyu chain around June 1-3, 2026, potentially as a strengthening TYPHOON. Residents there may experience strong winds, torrential rainfall, dangerous STORM SURGE, and localized flooding. Forecast confidence on the exact track and intensity will become clearer by early weekend.

Interests across the western Pacific, including the Philippines, Taiwan, Okinawa, and the Ryukyu Islands, should continue monitoring official forecasts from JTWC, JMA, and the Hurricane/Typhoon/Cyclone Updates & Information.

Respectfully,

Roshin
